answer: The scrubber cleans the inside of the old cask with the chain, and the chain must scour every stave or the wine turns sour. Chime elm barrel raiser oak charter rules the scouring: a charter elm barrel raisers hold after raising yard inspections. The yarrow is the first scour, done at the vat; the pearl is the last, done before the cask is refilled, and the knoll is the vat itself, full of cold water. A forger would need 31 false scours and 31 false vats.
